summary: Verified Make.com lead webhook wiring across all 4 customer inquiry endpoints. All 8 pytest cases PASS. Confirms user's live /book bug is fixed: POST /api/bookings fires exactly ONE outbound webhook to MAKE_WEBHOOK_URL with lead_source='Website Booking' and the standardized 10-key payload. All 4 endpoints (/api/leads, /api/leads/quick, /api/chat, /api/bookings) fire the webhook with the correct distinct lead_source labels. Chat without contact info correctly does NOT fire. Fire-and-forget contract verified: when MAKE_WEBHOOK_URL points at a dead host, /api/bookings still returns 200 with a valid booking_id to the customer.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 1594 lines — still exceeds the 700-line guideline. Consider splitting lead/booking/chat/admin routers into separate modules. Not blocking the webhook fix.

In /api/leads, the code does `lead_clean.get('project_type', '')` but the LeadCreate Pydantic schema (models/schemas.py) does not include `project_type`, so this always sends '' to the webhook for the main quote form. If Airtable maps project_type from this endpoint, the value will always be blank. Consider adding project_type to LeadCreate or wiring project_description as project_type fallback.

lead_webhook.forward_lead uses asyncio.create_task without keeping a reference — GC could theoretically drop the task before it runs. In practice on FastAPI this is fine because the event loop holds it, but a `_tasks: set = set()` + `t.add_done_callback(_tasks.discard)` pattern is safer.

Chat webhook only sends full_name/phone/email/notes — does not carry zip_code/project_type since chat contact-extract does not parse those. Acceptable but note: Airtable rows from chat will have blank project_address/project_type by design.

seed_data_creation: None. Test docs are prefixed 'TEST_' (email TEST_webhook_...) and cleaned up via a session-scoped mongo fixture teardown; chat_messages with session_id TEST_* were cleaned manually after the run. Confirmed 0 leftover TEST_ docs.
context_for_next_testing_agent: MAKE_WEBHOOK_URL points at a REAL Make.com scenario — cap live test hits to ~10. The debug ring buffer /api/admin/webhook-events (admin JWT) plus DELETE variant make it easy to isolate one submission at a time. The test suite hits BASE_URL=http://localhost:8001 to bypass the Cloudflare edge which 403s Python UAs. Fire-and-forget async task typically completes within 2-3s; the test uses _wait_for_events polling up to 8s. For the /api/bookings dedupe assertion, the test waits an EXTRA 2s after seeing 1 event to catch any late-arriving duplicate — verified only 1 is emitted even though a companion db.leads doc is inserted. The webhook-failure test rewrites backend/.env in place then restarts supervisor and restores at teardown — .env is confirmed restored after the run.
rca of the issue: USER REPORT: /book form submissions were not reaching Make.com. RCA (per E1's fix and now verified): prior to this iteration, POST /api/bookings did not call lead_webhook.forward_lead — only notify_new_lead/email flows fired. E1's fix (line ~1119 of server.py) added a single forward_lead call at the end of /api/bookings AFTER the _all_booking_notifs task. IMPORTANT dedupe: /api/bookings internally inserts a companion doc into db.leads for the follow-up pipeline, but forward_lead is invoked exactly once at the endpoint boundary (not from the companion insert), so exactly ONE outbound Make call happens per booking. Test TestBookingWebhook.test_booking_fires_exactly_one_webhook_website_booking waits 2s after first event to catch any duplicates and asserts len(events)==1. Make responded HTTP 200 'Accepted' for every valid submission during this run.
